title: About
text:
This site documents a project to build an AI player for city-building and business simulation games, in public, failures included. It also carries research notes: methods, papers, and things worth writing down.
This site is written in Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages. Posts are mirrored free on Substack. There is no paywall; if the writing ever earns anything, it will be through voluntary donations.

title: From one zone to a working city: the first two experiments
text:
No model managed a city in this post. Both experiments used fixed commands. That was deliberate. Before we judge any AI decision, the machinery must be trustworthy. A purchase must cost the right amount. A bad purchase must fail safely. Time must advance in a controlled way. A saved city must restore correctly.
Experiment E001 tested one purchase. Experiment E002 tested a small settlement. Together they form one progression. First, trust a single action. Then, trust many actions working together.

title: From one zone to a working city: the first two experiments
text:
E001: make one purchase trustworthy
A tile is the smallest square of the map. A zone is a marked area where buildings can develop. Buying a residential zone costs $100 in the game.
The test used a clear 32 by 32 map. It used easy difficulty and $20,000 of game money. One affordability case used only $99. Time-test disasters were off. A disaster is a random damaging event. We disabled them so results stayed comparable.

What a purchase does
A purchase has two stages. First, the tool prepares the site. It stages pending changes and a cost. Second, a funding check runs. It either discards the pending changes or applies them and deducts the money.
This two-stage design protects the city. A failed purchase must leave the real map and cash unchanged. That property is what E001 tested.


The twelve cases
The final suite had twelve cases. Each case verified one behaviour.

Staging leaves real state unchanged. A clear-site purchase then charges $100 and changes exactly nine expected residential tiles.
$99 cannot buy the $100 zone. Map and cash stay unchanged.
An anchor at (0,0) rejects a footprint outside the top and left bounds.
An anchor at (31,31) rejects a footprint outside the bottom and right bounds.
A blocked placement discards partial clearing. A later clear request has no stale fee.
One eligible tree adds $1. Total cost is $101.
A duplicate zone purchase is rejected without another charge.
Saved map and budget fields restore after construction.
One hundred paused time steps do not advance city time.
Nonzero saved flags and loaded map bounds survive, including a dimension change.
768 internal phases reach time 48 and January 1901 from the start.
Construction, one-year advancement, and load restore all compared simulation fields.

A flag is an on/off property stored in a binary digit of a tile value. For example, one flag marks a zone centre. Another marks whether a tile has power. Restoration checks must compare raw values and flags, not only the displayed tile type. A tile can conduct electricity without having supply. Those are different states.


Two failures, two repairs
The unchanged game passed 8 of the original 10 cases. Two failures were reproduced and repaired.
First, map loading kept stale flags. The value setter preserved existing flags when the incoming saved value had none. Loading a clean snapshot over constructed tiles could leave old zone flags behind. The repair rebuilds tile objects from ID and flags, and rebuilds map bounds.
Second, census stepping failed. The census code used a budget name that was not defined in that context. The two census calls were corrected to pass the simulation’s budget explicitly.
Two checks were added during diagnosis. The repaired suite passed 12 of 12. Do not read this as the original ten tests passing unchanged. The repairs are part of the result.


Browser checks
We also checked the game in a browser. A disposable test city was used. A residential placement in the original build charged $101. After rebuilding with repairs, a fresh placement charged $102. Both charges fit one or two $1 clearing fees. The controlled clear-map test independently verified the $100 base cost.
The upstream test suite was also run. 160 of 162 upstream tests passed. Two bounds tests still fail. They expect zero width and height to trigger an assertion. Their source and tests were unchanged. The full upstream suite is not green. We do not claim otherwise.
E001 established a small set of trustworthy operations. It did not establish city growth, good planning, or AI skill.

title: From one zone to a working city: the first two experiments
section: E002: operate a small developing settlement
text:
E002: operate a small developing settlement
E002 asked a bigger question. Can normal purchases, power, transport, controlled time, and observations work together in a settlement that develops?
Each trial created a fresh clear 64 by 64 map. Settings were easy difficulty, $20,000, 7% tax, automatic budget, full service percentages, slow speed, and disasters off. There were three trials each for three layouts: complete, no-power, and no-roads. Global randomness was unseeded. Results are diagnostic observations, not precise causal estimates.

The exact layout



Asset
Position




Coal plant
Anchor (46,12), 4 by 4 tiles


Residential zones
Anchors (12,26), (15,26), (18,26)


Commercial zones
Anchors (24,26), (27,26)


Industrial zones
Anchors (36,26), (39,26), (42,26)


Road
33 tiles along y = 28, x = 11 to 43


Horizontal wire
35 tiles along y = 24, x = 12 to 46


Vertical wire
9 tiles along x = 46, y = 15 to 23



The road sits below the zones. The wire sits above them. Industry sits east of housing. Coal was the cheaper power source for this connection test. It also adds pollution. The layout was not optimized for city health.
Complete construction cost $4,350. That left $15,650. The no-power layout cost $1,350. The no-roads layout cost $4,020. Wires stayed in all layouts.
Each trial advanced two years: 1,536 internal phases, to January 1902. Each trial recorded 25 observations: initial and monthly. The final nine-trial run recorded 672 purchases and 225 observations.


What was measured
The driver recorded each command and charge. It recorded direct map population indices for residential, commercial, and industrial zones. An index is an engine number, not a count of people. Displayed population uses different scaling and updates on its own schedule. Do not mix these measures into one series without explaining units and timing.
It also recorded developed-zone counts, zone power, census and evaluation values, demand, cash, pollution scores, traffic density, and annual tax events.


The first run failed, and growth hid the fault
The first run passed 3 of 9 trials. All complete layouts grew. But every traffic request returned no route. The three complete trials made 38, 47, and 63 requests with zero success.
This is the most important lesson of E002. Visible growth concealed a broken system. A city can look alive while its transport simulation silently fails. Measurement caught what watching would have missed.


A test-design mistake of our own
The no-power layouts stayed empty and made no traffic requests. The original test still required successful traffic in those layouts. That was an assistant test-design mistake. An empty unpowered city cannot generate traffic.
The requirement was removed for no-power controls in a dated amendment. Complete layouts still had to show routes. Road-free layouts still had to report missing roads. Original files and results remain preserved. The final result includes both an engine repair and a justified changed control requirement. It is not nine unchanged tests passing after only an engine fix.


The traffic diagnosis: three small faults
A separate fixture placed a residential and a commercial zone beside a five-tile road. Four checks covered numeric drive coordinates, a known route, traffic density, and the no-road control.








Stage
Passing checks
Fault exposed




Original traffic code
1 of 4
A position object was passed where separate x and y numbers were required, so valid movement could not happen


Initial copy fixed
1 of 4
Valid movement then exposed an undefined variable


Movement fixed
2 of 4
A route reached its destination, but invalid stacked coordinates prevented density recording


Stack copy fixed
4 of 4
Numeric coordinates, route, density, and missing-road checks all pass



The three corrected expressions were:
var drivePos = new Position(startPos.x, startPos.y);
drivePos = Position.move(drivePos, dir);
this._stack.push(new Position(drivePos.x, drivePos.y));
These fixes follow the position interface. They do not redesign route distance, random direction choice, prices, or growth probabilities. Complex traffic behaviour beyond these checks remains untested.


Final nine-trial observations
All final trials passed the revised checks. Each reached the date, reconciled cash, and applied every purchase at its expected cost. All eight original zones had power in complete and no-road trials. None had power in no-power trials.

Road-free trials returned 6, 4, and 4 missing-road results. Their peak residential index was 2 each. Some transient industrial development also appeared. Missing roads did not prevent every initial growth event.
No commercial development appeared at any monthly observation. Industry satisfied the predefined employment-growth requirement. A route can end beside a commercial zone before that zone develops. Do not claim commercial economic activity was validated.


Money
After construction, complete cities started with $15,650. Over two years, their combined annual cash changes were -$20, -$2, and -$4. One second-year event was positive. All three had small net operating losses over the full window.
The engine suppresses normal maintenance spending before its population index is established. Some empty-city annual events therefore changed no cash despite a calculated maintenance requirement. That does not mean roads are free.
Controls had different reserves and pollution because they bought different assets. Removing the coal plant changes pollution as well as power. Three unseeded trials cannot separate those effects precisely.
After the traffic fix, E001 still passed 12 of 12. Upstream tests stayed at 160 of 162. The production build passed with the same three warnings. The traffic-repaired bundle was compiled but not separately verified in the browser.

title: From one zone to a working city: the first two experiments
section: What E002 proved, and what it did not
text:
What E002 proved, and what it did not
E002 proved a functioning, observable engineering loop. Purchases, power, roads, time, and measurements work together. It did not prove balanced city health, commercial growth, profitability, or long-term survival.
Growth alone would have hidden the traffic fault. That is why we test before we judge. The next post finally lets the model choose. It chooses exactly one action. The action is legal. It still fails.
Technical details for this post are in the shared appendix. The next post covers E003: the first model-selected command and its failed repair.

text:
Can one model request choose a useful repair? Can the test setup execute that exact command? Does power reach all eight existing zones within one simulated month?
This was the first time the model selected a game action. Everything before this used fixed commands. That distinction matters. E001 and E002 tested machinery. E003 tests a decision.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
text:
The fixture
The adapter rebuilt the complete layout from E002, but omitted one wire at (46,19). Construction cost $4,345, leaving $15,655. The city then advanced one month, so power scans established the fault. The observation date was February 1900. All eight original zones were unpowered. A coal plant existed.
Before spending anything on the model, six local checks passed:







Check
Result




Known fault and reference repair
One $5 wire at (46,19) restores all eight zones after another month


Wait control
Zones stay unpowered; no charge


Invalid coordinate
Rejected without changing map or cash


Insufficient funds
Rejected without changing map or cash


Occupied plant site
The normal wire tool rejects the site without charging


Second command in one episode
Rejected without further change



The reference repair ran in a separate local fixture. It was not applied to the model’s live city after failure. That separation matters. The live city kept its failure intact for honest reporting.
The live episode created a fresh fixture and kept it in memory while waiting for the response. It did not save and reload an old simulation across the network request.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
section: What the model saw, and what it could do
text:
What the model saw, and what it could do
The model received cash, date, demand, the plant count, zone coordinates and power states, and a text map. The map covered x = 8 to 50 and y = 10 to 30. It had an explicit list of x-columns and y-labelled row strings. Symbols were . for clear ground, P for plant, W for wire, R, C, I for zones, and = for road.
It also received tool prices, conduction rules, a $50 in-game action allowance, and the goal to restore supply with one legal action. It could choose wire, road, or wait. Waiting used (0,0) as unused coordinates.
The known missing-wire coordinate was not supplied as the answer. The gap is visible in the map data. The replay’s red and gold outlines were added later for human explanation. The model saw text, not those annotated pictures.
Be clear about the assistance here. This was a known power problem, a small map, a restricted action set, and no need to explore. It is not unrestricted management. It still required selecting an effective coordinate.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
text:
The exact returned command
{
  "tool": "wire",
  "x": 44,
  "y": 15,
  "explanation": "Extend the plant's existing wire toward the industrial zones; this is the first link in restoring power."
}
This is the model’s returned command and short visible explanation. It is not a private internal reasoning trace. We have no access to such a trace, and we do not claim to know the model’s internal reasoning.
The controller validated the fields, types, coordinate window, affordability, and staged cost. It used the normal wire tool for site checks and application. It accepted the action, changed exactly (44,15) from clear ground to wire, and charged $5. Cash fell from $15,655 to $15,650.
The existing vertical wire is at x = 46. The chosen tile at (44,15) is two tiles west of that line. It has no cardinal connection to it or to the plant. Cardinal means sharing an edge: up, down, left, or right. Diagonal contact does not conduct power. The chosen tile does not close the gap at (46,19).
After another month, all eight zones remained unpowered. The endpoint was March 1900. The model explanation described a first step, even though the task required a complete repair in one action.







Result layer
Outcome




API returns a completed response with one function call
Pass


Requested command is legal and executed exactly, with correct charge
Pass


All eight original zones have power within the follow-up window
Fail: 0 of 8



The live process exited with code 1 because the repair criterion failed. This is a completed failed experiment, not an unfinished connection. No second request, hidden repair, changed success criterion, or replacement command was used.

No seed or temperature override was specified. Do not infer reproducible model decisions from the model name alone. The same request might return a different action another time.
The client created a request-start marker with exclusive file mode before sending. The launcher refuses a directory with that marker. A timeout can leave the provider outcome unknown, so a request is not repeated automatically. These controls bound the episode to one paid request. They are not a recurring monthly spending limit.
No key was configured in process, user, or machine environment during preflight. The key was entered in a masked local window. It passed through memory and was not recorded in the prompt, arguments, source, or evidence.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
section: What this result does and does not show
text:
What this result does and does not show
The result establishes a model-to-game command connection. Format, legality, exact execution, and task success were checked separately. The first three passed. The last failed. That separation is the point of the experiment design.
The result does not establish reliable decision quality. The cause of the poor choice is unresolved. Character-map indexing, task wording, spatial inference, and interpreting the one-action objective are all hypotheses. One attempt cannot show which mattered. It cannot show whether a different model would succeed, or whether more reasoning would help.
The proposed next step is to test an explicit wire-coordinate or connected-segment observation format. No E004, revised-prompt comparison, second paid repair, or expanded action budget has been run or accepted as a complete protocol.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
text:
Watching the process
The user asked to watch the playing process. That request exposed a gap. E002 had complete action records and monthly measurements, but no live video or full intermediate maps. Its 59-second video is a retrospective reconstruction, not recovered footage. It reissued the first trial’s 86 purchases through the real game tools and matched every cost. Monthly measurements appear as a chart. Monthly map images were not invented.
E003 improved capture. Twelve full state records cover construction, warm-up, the model observation, the action result, follow-up, and endpoint. Its 47-second video uses those actual states and the returned command. It runs no new trajectory and makes no model call. Playback pacing is editorial. An earlier 55-second draft wrongly included warm-up states after the action. It was preserved and corrected. Use the 47-second version.
Both videos use upstream MicropolisJS tile artwork. License files were copied with the delivered media. Check those licenses before publishing any assets.

title: A legal move that did not repair the city
text:
What remains open
Several questions stay open, and the blog should not pretend otherwise.

What do “flourish” and city health mean in numbers? No target population, reserve, pollution limit, or sustained-profit requirement is accepted yet.
What should the model see? Individual placements, candidate actions, road and zone batches, or district-level commands are all still undecided.
Would a clearer state representation improve repair selection? That needs repeat counts and comparison rules fixed before claiming an effect.
What spending controls should future work use? E003’s single authorized request is complete.
How do we build a general reference player and a fair comparison? Neither exists yet.
Can we validate commercial growth, broader transport, long-term finance, and larger scenarios? Not yet.
What about a local model or cluster? No such model or hardware has been installed. That choice needs a concrete need and measurement first.

The honest summary of the project so far is short. The machinery works. The settlement develops under fixed commands. The first model decision was legal, exact, and wrong. That is progress, because now we can measure the next attempt against it.
Technical details for this post are in the shared appendix.

title: Technical appendix: experiments through E003
text: This appendix supports the E001/E002 and E003 posts. It records implementation, not a request to run it. The E000 introduction will be written by the owner.

title: Technical appendix: experiments through E003
text:
Data flow
Human browser input -> Game.handleTool -> normal tools -> simulation

E001/E002 Node driver -> imported normal tools -> separate simulation

E003 observation -> one OpenAI request -> function-call arguments
                -> local validation -> normal tool -> same in-memory simulation
                -> fixed time advancement -> saved observations/full maps

Saved evidence -> Python/Pillow rendering -> FFmpeg MP4
The first API utility is independent of the game. The browser game and Node test instances are independent of each other. The renderer never controls the game. E003 is the point where a model response first selects a game action.

title: Technical appendix: experiments through E003
text:
Build and test commands
Working directory for game installation and build: the local micropolisJS checkout. The install used a bundled package manager to supply pinned npm. Production build:
node .\node_modules\webpack-cli\bin\cli.js --mode production
Static server, using the bundled Python runtime:
& $pythonExe -m http.server 5173 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory <path to the micropolisJS dist folder>
From the project root, the recorded experiment and test entry points are:
node .\scripts\run-game-experiment.cjs
node .\scripts\run-settlement-experiment.cjs
node .\scripts\run-settlement-experiment.cjs --traffic-diagnostic
node .\micropolisJS\node_modules\jest\bin\jest.js --config .\scripts\upstream-tests.config.cjs --runInBand
node .\scripts\run-llm-repair.cjs
The final command defaults to local-only E003 preflight. It is not the paid live launcher. The completed live directory refuses another paid attempt. These commands are references. They were not rerun to assemble the writer handoff.
The Node harness uses Webpack with Node target, resolves .js and .ts imports, uses the game’s TypeScript loader and config, and writes a CommonJS bundle under a local .cache build directory. The game’s TypeScript config uses ES5 target, CommonJS module compilation, allowJs, and strict checks.
E001 and E002 test children have 30-second execution timeouts. E003 has 30 seconds for local preflight and 45 seconds for the live child, with its own 30-second HTTP deadline. Compilation sits outside those child execution timeouts.

title: Technical appendix: experiments through E003
section: Claims to keep, and claims to avoid
text:
Claims to keep, and claims to avoid
Safe, with qualifications: the model API connection works; the test setup places constructions with normal rules and costs on tested tools and sites; the repaired engine develops a scripted settlement in fixed small layouts; traffic works in the tested repaired paths; saved fields restored in E001; the first hosted model game command reached the game; that action was legal and executed correctly but failed to restore power; recorded project API spending was very small.
Do not claim: the LLM built or managed the E001/E002 cities; a balanced, profitable, self-sustaining AI city manager exists; E003 repaired power or succeeded on a later retry; the known scripted repair was the model’s choice; all upstream tests pass; a single failed model choice proves a particular prompt, map, or model weakness; a game task validates real-company management; the videos are original live screen recordings.
